correctness.rationale: The replacement retains the formulas and makes the Euclidean check explicit. With p=(n−1)/2, U=sin²(δ/2) has Beta(p,p) law. On the radial deficit triangle, factor the exact cosine-law numerator by ε−A−B: this gives Q=(ε−A−B)/(4c) times 1+O(ε) uniformly even up to the triangle edge. The beta-CDF expansion and smooth radial densities give relative O(ε) under integration. The scaled angular density integrates to B(p,3)/4 before multiplying by f², the angle-density constant and c^(−p); changing z to z² gives the stated Dirichlet parameters. The flat cosine law gives the same limit directly with f=n/T and c=T/4. Both monotonic factors have the asserted signs, including strictness since n≥2, and c→0 with f bounded below ensures the range is unbounded. For n=3, multiplying the uniform angular cutoff by the two radial densities and then integrating in the radial difference gives the factor 1/(4J²); the resulting domain includes L=T and gives zero at L=2T. An independent bounded lens check used the 3D separation density sinh²(κd)/J² times the integral from d/2 to T of sinh²(κr)−tanh(κd/2)sinh(κr)cosh(κr), from the bisector cap and the ball-overlap identity. Composite Simpson quadrature at κ=T=1 and ε=0.005 gave 3.13176015874e−7 by both routes. The checker and recorded 36 assertions are supplementary evidence, not a fresh run or a proof.
